solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lens cover English priest found in yard

parts.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English

indicators.note: something found in a place sits inside it, so the priest goes within the yard letters

parts.note: YD is the abbreviation for a yard
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Old Testament, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: An English clergyman turns up in a yard, holding something that protects a camera lens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lens' suggests a camera, but the eye has a lens too, and that is the one covered here.
explanation.definitionFit: The eyelid is the fold of skin that shuts over the eye, playfully called a cover for its lens.

clue.text: Carve eminent theologian's initials on church

indicators.note: initials are the opening letters of a person's names, so only the first letter of each word is kept

parts.note: the first letters of the two words
CH is the usual abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone cuts a great divine's monogram into a church wall.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to cut a design into a surface, a close synonym of carve.

clue.text: Agent infiltrating capital upset powerful figure

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so the combined letters are read from the bottom
an agent who infiltrates gets inside an organisation, so these letters are placed within the city

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital
a rep, or representative, acts as an agent for a firm

explanation.surface: A spy works inside a capital city and topples the strongman ruling it.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal acts on the whole combination, not just the city, once the agent is inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is the supreme ruler of an empire, as powerful a figure as there is.

clue.text: Your uncle slid off in a suspicious manner

indicators.note: letters that have slid off their places have lost their order and must be rearranged

parts.note: all thirteen letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A relative sneaks away from a gathering in a way that arouses suspicion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slid' does double duty: its letters join the fodder, and 'slid off' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Incredulously means with disbelief, as a suspicious, doubting person reacts.

clue.text: Flipping fanatic screening old PG movie

indicators.note: to screen something is to shield it by surrounding it, so the outer word wraps the others
to flip something is to turn it over, so the word for the zealot is written backwards

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast or fanatic, as in a fitness nut
O is the abbreviation for old
taken as written

explanation.surface: An irate zealot tries to block the showing of an old family-rated film.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed TUN surrounds O and PG: T(OPG)UN. PG is the British and American film rating for parental guidance.
explanation.definitionFit: Top Gun is the 1986 Tom Cruise film about naval fighter pilots, itself rated PG.

clue.text: Choose to join housing agency? It's a job!

indicators.note: a building housing something holds it inside, so the American spy agency goes within the last word of the phrase

parts.note: to opt in is to choose to join a scheme
the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency

explanation.surface: A recruit choosing to sign up with a spy agency announces their new posting.
explanation.walkthrough: OPT IN holds CIA: OPTI(CIA)N. The definition is deliberately vague; the answer is simply one of many occupations.
explanation.definitionFit: An optician is a trade or profession, so it is indeed a job, the definition being a whimsical category.

clue.text: Stripped android with electronic instrument

indicators.note: something stripped has had its outer covering taken off, so the first and last letters are removed

parts.note: an android is a humanoid robot
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: A disassembled droid fitted with a synthesiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'electronic instrument' reads as one phrase, a synthesiser; split it, and 'instrument' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument of the orchestra.

clue.text: Drink on completely empty stomach?

parts.note: beer is a drink
to gut a building or fish is to empty it completely

explanation.surface: Is it wise to drink alcohol when you have not eaten anything?
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty stomach' looks like a single phrase, but 'stomach' alone is the definition and 'completely empty' is the verb gut.
explanation.definitionFit: A beer gut is the paunchy belly blamed on heavy drinking, so a kind of stomach.

clue.text: Serenity of India encapsulated by my antique bust

indicators.note: a thing encapsulated by another is enclosed within it, so the single letter sits inside the rest
something bust is broken, so the pieces are put back together in a new order

parts.note: the nine letters of these two words
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An antique bust from India radiates a calm, serene expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bust' pretends to be a sculpted head, the antique itself; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Equanimity is calmness and composure of mind, a near synonym of serenity.

clue.text: Staunch Unionist ousted by a predatory beast

indicators.note: someone ousted by a rival is thrown out and replaced, so one letter makes way for another

parts.note: stout means staunch or resolute, as in a stout defender
U is the abbreviation for Unionist
taken as written

explanation.surface: A loyal Unionist politician is driven out by a ruthless rival.
explanation.walkthrough: In STOUT the U is swapped for A. Unionist refers to Northern Irish parties loyal to the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: The stoat is a small carnivorous mammal of the weasel family that hunts rabbits.

clue.text: Plagiarist reticent about origin of published article in court

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shy word goes round the single letter

parts.note: coy means shy or reticent

indicators.note: the origin of a word is where it begins, so only its first letter is used

parts.note: the first letter

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the article goes within the abbreviation for court

parts.note: CT is the abbreviation for court
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A shy writer accused of plagiarism is in court over the source of a published piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A copycat is someone who imitates another, as a plagiarist copies another's words.

clue.text: Some notable Australian actors still on the stage?

indicators.note: some of a phrase is only part of it, so the answer is a run of letters inside the words

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A remark about a few distinguished Australian performers who are still working in theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like 'yet', but it means motionless: the actors hold a frozen pose.
explanation.definitionFit: A tableau is a scene in which performers stand silent and motionless, as if in a picture.

clue.text: Bishop prepared fit gunner for sacrifice

parts.note: B is the chess notation for a bishop

indicators.note: something prepared has been made ready by working on it, so the letters that follow are reworked

parts.note: all twelve letters of these words

explanation.surface: A bishop gets a strong artilleryman ready to be sacrificed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' looks like a link to the definition, but its letters belong in the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A burnt offering is an animal or food burnt on an altar as a gift to a god, a sacrifice.

clue.text: Contractor from country bordering Spain regularly deals with king

indicators.note: to border something is to lie around its edges, so the country's letters enclose the others

parts.note: France borders Spain to the north
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the second and fourth letters
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A contractor working from France, next to Spain, does business with the king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country bordering Spain' reads as one description of France, but the country also wraps around Spain's letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: A freelancer works under contract for various clients rather than as an employee.

clue.text: See 4
Maintain state enclosing favourite area ultimately spoilt atmosphere

indicators.note: enclosing means surrounding, so the state's letters go around the pet word

parts.note: Peru is a South American state
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
A is the abbreviation for area

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letters of the two words are kept

parts.note: the last letter of each word

explanation.surface: A country keeps its beloved region going even as its air becomes polluted.
explanation.definitionFit: To perpetuate is to make something continue indefinitely, so to keep it up or maintain it.

clue.text: United supporter set about breaking journalist's listening device

indicators.note: something breaking another splits it open and lodges inside it

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the journalist in charge

indicators.note: to set something about is to turn it round, so the garment word faces the other way

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names
a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A Manchester United fan attacks a reporter and grabs his recording gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter' looks like a football fan of United; it is an undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: An earbud is a tiny earphone that sits in the ear, a device for listening to audio.

clue.text: Frisky tomcat patrols university stalking female? He does all sorts!

indicators.note: a stalker follows behind, so this group comes after the letter for female

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female

indicators.note: a guard patrols an area by going all round it, so the shuffled letters surround the next one
a frisky animal leaps about, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: the six letters of the word
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A randy tomcat prowls the campus, following a female around.
explanation.definitionFit: A factotum is a person employed to do all kinds of jobs, from Latin for 'do everything'.

clue.text: Company setting new mark in genuine food

indicators.note: the word genuine is setting the other letters as a jeweller sets a stone, holding them inside

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
real means genuine
N is the abbreviation for new
M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A firm sets a fresh quality mark on authentic food products.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornmeal is flour ground from maize, used in breads and polenta, so a foodstuff.

clue.text: Expert Charlie introduced to implement standard practice

parts.note: a pro, short for professional, is an expert

indicators.note: something introduced to another is put into it, so the single letter goes within the tool word

parts.note: a tool is an implement
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A consultant named Charlie is brought in to put the usual procedures into effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'implement' looks like a verb, as in putting a plan into effect, but it is the noun tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A protocol is an established code of procedure, the accepted way of doing things.

clue.text: Partially quell a revolutionary uprising for general

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising up means reading from the bottom upwards
partially means only in part, so the answer is just part of the words that follow

parts.note: the end of the first word, the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A general half-succeeds in suppressing a rebel's uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'general' looks like the army officer suppressing the revolt; it is the adjective meaning comprehensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Overall as an adjective means taking everything into account, so general or total.

clue.text: On the surface, note is filled with love

indicators.note: something filled with a substance has it inside, so the zero letter goes within the note

parts.note: A flat is a musical note
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Outwardly, a letter is overflowing with affection.
explanation.walkthrough: A FLAT, a two-word note, holds O: AFL(O)AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Afloat means floating on water rather than sinking, so on the surface.

clue.text: Odd parts of orbit around Earth become noticeable

indicators.note: the odd parts are the letters in the first, third, fifth positions and so on

parts.note: letters one, three, five, seven, nine and eleven of the two words
E is the abbreviation for Earth

explanation.surface: Strange sections of a satellite's path around the planet start to stand out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a container signal; it is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtrude is to become noticeable in an unwelcome way, pushing oneself forward.

clue.text: Compare primitive plant-like species on the radio

indicators.note: something heard on the radio is heard rather than seen, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a lichen is a simple organism of fungus and alga, once thought a primitive plant

explanation.surface: A radio show compares a simple plant-like organism with other species.
explanation.definitionFit: To liken one thing to another is to compare them or point out their resemblance.

clue.text: Infection husband caught in Tenerife on vacation was airborne, reportedly

indicators.note: something caught in another is trapped inside it
a word on vacation has been vacated, emptied of its middle, so only its outer letters stay

parts.note: the first and last letters
H is the abbreviation for husband

indicators.note: reportedly means as people say it, so the word is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: flew is the past tense of fly, to be airborne

explanation.surface: A husband catches a bug on holiday in Tenerife, spread through the air, people say.
explanation.walkthrough: T(H)E, then FLU. Tenerife is a Spanish island popular with British holidaymakers.
explanation.definitionFit: The flu, short for influenza, is a common viral infection of the respiratory system.

clue.text: Feelings transmitted by knight in troubled times

parts.note: a transmitted message has been sent

indicators.note: the knight is placed in, inside, the jumbled letters
troubled things are disturbed, so these letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: the five letters of the word
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: Emotions are broadcast by a chivalrous hero in difficult days.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentiments are views or attitudes coloured by emotion, so feelings.

clue.text: What Steerpike does gets harder

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Steerpike is this puzzle's setter, who compiles crosswords
second meaning: concrete or jelly solidifies

explanation.walkthrough: Steerpike is the pseudonym of this crossword's compiler, so the first half points at the setter's own job.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter sets puzzles, and something that sets becomes firm or solid as it cools or dries.

clue.text: Obsessively orderly youths emptied Earl's study

parts.note: anal is slang for fussily obsessed with order and detail

indicators.note: a word that has been emptied has lost its insides, so only its outer letters stay

parts.note: the first and last letters
E is the abbreviation for earl; the 's links on to the definition

explanation.surface: Fussy, tidy young people have cleared out the earl's private library.
explanation.walkthrough: 'study' looks like the earl's room, but it is a verb meaning to examine.
explanation.definitionFit: To analyse something is to examine it in detail, which is to study it closely.

clue.text: Saga tours are essentially end of line for hedonist

parts.note: a saga is a long epic story

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so the middle letter of each word is taken

parts.note: the middle letter of each word

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: Saga holidays, aimed at older travellers, mark the end of the road for a pleasure-seeker.
explanation.walkthrough: Saga is a British company running holidays for the over-50s, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure is a person devoted to refined pleasures, especially food and wine, much like a hedonist.

clue.text: Slippery characters shelter retired soprano

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw or go back, so the shelter word is read in the backward direction

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
S is the abbreviation for soprano

explanation.surface: Dodgy types give refuge to an elderly singer who has stopped performing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' seems to describe the soprano, but it acts on the shelter word.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are literally slippery fish, and 'slippery characters' also suggests untrustworthy people.

clue.text: See 24
Giant move forward doesn't include Puerto Rico

indicators.note: a word that doesn't include something leaves it out, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: to progress is to move forward
PR is the abbreviation for Puerto Rico

explanation.surface: A huge step ahead that leaves out the Caribbean island.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogress is a female ogre, a monstrous giant of folklore.
